Description:
**Department:** Development

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Position:** Director of Development

**Employment Type:** Full\-time, exempt, salaried and benefited

**Agency Description:** We provide affordable, bilingual, and accessible mental health services for people of all ages living in Napa County. Our vision is to create a community of enduring strength by equipping children, youth, adults, and seniors with the tools they need to live emotionally healthy and stable lives through programs ranging from prevention to mental health treatment.

**Position Summary:** The Development Director (DD) leads and oversees all aspects of the agency’s philanthropic and communications activities. Working closely with the Executive Director, Executive Leadership team, Board of Directors, and Development staff, the DD drives dynamic development, builds donor relationships, and marketing strategies that meet and exceed the agency’s goals.


**Duties and Responsibilities**


Leadership \& Strategy

* Works closely with Executive Director, Leadership Team, and Board Development Committee to create and implement annual and long\-term development and marketing strategies that help meet and exceed the agency’s revenue, service delivery, and community engagement goals.
* Leads Board Development/Stewardship Committee, strategically leveraging its membership to support community engagement and fundraising initiatives
* Strategically supports Marketing Committee
* Develop and monitor annual Development revenue targets and expense budget with an eye toward maximizing fundraising efficiency and ROI on expenses.


Gifts and Philanthropy

* Develop and cultivate donor relationships as well as solicit funds.
* Leads Mentis giving program, working closely with ED, Board, and Development committee to ensure regular (at least quarterly) engagement with all donors.
* Builds, sustains, and models a culture of stewardship, emphasizing long\-term relationship\-building over continual asking.
* Manages a personal portfolio of donors in conjunction with ED as well as supports ED with ongoing major donor engagement.
* Works with ED, Board, and Development committee to continually identify and cultivate potential new major donors.


Events and Fundraising

* Oversee execution of Mentis’ community engagement events, including Jeffersonian Dinner series, Blue Skies Ahead reception, Mental Health Awareness Month event, Donor breakfast, and potential other events, and annual fundraising campaigns, including end\-of\-year giving, monthly giving, Mental Health Awareness Month, Suicide Prevention Month, and others throughout the year.

* Coordinate with program staff where needed to gather program data and other content for grant proposals and reports.


Communications \& Marketing

* Work with the Development Team to develop an engaging annual communications strategy and plan that meets the agency’s community engagement and fundraising goals.
* Support Development Team in creating and publishing engaging materials for a variety of audiences—including press releases, columns, media pitches, e\-blasts, advertisements, radio features, event promotion materials, impact reports, and more.
* Serve as Mentis spokesperson along with other directors and board members, representing the agency in public through presentations, media interviews, and local event attendance.


Administration

* Develop and monitor annual development budget in conjunction with ED and Finance Director.
* Work with Development Team to analyze monthly reports on fundraising revenue and progress toward goals.

* Encourage and provide professional growth opportunities.

jobs.description:
Come join the fun and make a difference with Discovery Cube! For over 25 years, we've been inspiring kids and educators alike with our hands\-on science education initiatives and interactive exhibits. Our four core initiatives \- STEM proficiency, early childhood education, healthy living, and environmental stewardship \- are future\-forward in promoting life\-long\-learning. Plus, with our immersive campuses in Orange County and Los Angeles, as well as our educational outreach programs, there are endless opportunities for learning exploration. As a prominent advocate for modern science education, we believe in empowering our learners with real\-world applications and spotlighting science as a solution and force for good. Don't miss out on the excitement and join our important mission today!

**Position:**



The Director of Corporate Relations is responsible for developing and managing corporate partnerships and fundraising initiatives that generate philanthropic support for Discovery Cube's mission, programs, exhibits, events, and educational initiatives. This position manages a portfolio of current and prospective corporate partners and leads strategies to identify new funding opportunities, cultivate relationships, secure corporate gifts and sponsorships, and steward existing partners to support retention and long\-term engagement.



The Director also plays a key role in the strategy and execution of fundraising events, including securing sponsorships, in\-kind support, and other event revenue. The position is accountable for achieving established corporate and event fundraising goals and maintaining a strong pipeline of prospective and renewing partners.



Working collaboratively with Development leadership and departments across the organization, the Director develops compelling opportunities that align Discovery Cube's mission and organizational priorities with the philanthropic, community engagement, and sponsorship goals of corporate partners.


**Responsibilities:**


**Corporate Fundraising \& Partnership Development**


* Manage a portfolio of current and prospective corporate partners, developing individualized strategies for cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal.
* Identify, research, qualify, cultivate, and solicit new corporate prospects to expand Discovery Cube's corporate funding base and build a strong pipeline of prospective partners.
* Secure corporate support through philanthropic gifts, sponsorships, grants, underwriting opportunities, in\-kind contributions, and other strategic partnerships.
* Identify opportunities to increase the level of support and engagement of existing corporate partners and strengthen long\-term relationships.
* Develop annual strategies and action plans for assigned corporate fundraising initiatives, including prospecting, cultivation, solicitation, renewals, and stewardship to achieve established annual corporate fundraising goals.
* Stay informed of corporate philanthropy, community engagement, sponsorship, and funding opportunities that align with Discovery Cube's mission and organizational priorities.


**Corporate Relationship Management \& Stewardship**


* Develop and maintain strong, long\-term relationships with corporate partners, prospects, executives, community leaders, and other key stakeholders.

* Collaborate with internal departments to coordinate and fulfill corporate sponsorship benefits and partnership commitments.

* Develop compelling sponsorship proposals, corporate funding requests, presentations, and other solicitation materials tailored to prospective partners.
* Identify Discovery Cube programs, exhibits, events, and educational initiatives that present strong opportunities for corporate sponsorship and philanthropic investment.
* Partner with program and organizational leaders to understand funding priorities and translate organizational needs into compelling corporate partnership opportunities.
* Research corporate giving programs and grant opportunities and prepare assigned corporate grant applications and proposals.

jobs.description:
***“Every person deserves compassion, dignity, and the safety of a place to call home.”***
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*Homelessness is the largest social and public health crisis in California. Illumination Health \+ Home is a growing non\-profit organization dedicated towards disrupting the cycle of homelessness by providing targeted, interdisciplinary services in our recuperative care centers, emergency shelters, housing services and children's and family programs. IH\+H currently has 13\+ facilities with 22\+ micro\-communities scattered across Orange County, Los Angeles County and the Inland Empire.*

**The Opportunity**


We are seeking a strategic, hands\-on Vice President of Development to lead and grow our philanthropic revenue while building a high\-performing, mission\-driven team. Reporting to the CEO and serving on the executive leadership team, you will shape and execute a multi\-year fundraising strategy spanning major gifts, individual giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, special events, Board engagement, and campaign development.


This is a leadership role for a fundraiser who loves both the work and the people. You will set strategy and lead a team, while personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors and philanthropic partners.  

  

The pay range for this position is **$155,000 \- $175,000 annually**, depending on experience.  

  

**What you'll do**


Fundraising Strategy \& Revenue Growth* Develop and execute a three\-year comprehensive fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities, with annual goals by revenue stream and quarterly revenue, pipeline, and activity targets.
* Maintain a fundraising pipeline sufficient to support 2–3 times the annual major\-gift and institutional goals, and identify opportunities to diversify revenue and grow unrestricted support.
* Monitor performance and provide the CEO and Board with regular reports on revenue, pipeline, projections, and progress, partnering with Finance on accurate forecasts.

  

Major Gifts \& Individual Philanthropy

* Build and personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors, developing individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies.
* Personally lead or participate in five\-, six\-, and seven\-figure solicitations, and grow the number and value of major gifts.
* Develop compelling cases for support, and partner with the CEO and Board to identify and engage high\-capacity individuals and community influencers.
* Build and deepen relationships with corporations, foundations, and institutional partners, moving funders from transactional grants toward strategic, multi\-year partnerships.

  

Corporate, Foundation \& Board Engagement

* Build and deepen relationships with corporations, foundations, and institutional partners, moving funders from transactional grants toward strategic, multi\-year partnerships.
* Partner with the CEO and Board to maximize their effectiveness as ambassadors and fundraisers, setting clear annual engagement expectations and providing tools, coaching, and meeting preparation.
* Create opportunities for Board members to leverage their networks to expand the donor base.

  

Donor Stewardship \& Campaigns

* Design and lead a comprehensive stewardship strategy, with a goal of increasing donor retention by at least 5% in the first year.
* Drive donor upgrades, recurring and multi\-year giving, and re\-engagement of lapsed donors, ensuring donors receive timely, meaningful communication about their impact.
* Assess organizational readiness for future capital and transformational campaigns, completing a campaign readiness assessment within the first six months.

  

Team Leadership \& Operations

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of seven, setting clear goals and expectations and fostering a culture that is collaborative, supportive, accountable, and donor\-centered.
* Lead with kindness, humility, professionalism, and respect while maintaining high standards, and encourage collaboration across Finance, Programs, Marketing, and Executive Leadership.
* Ensure the CRM is fully utilized for fundraising management, with standardized dashboards, reliable monthly and quarterly forecasting, and accurate reporting in partnership with Finance.

 **What you'll bring**

* Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
* 8–10\+ years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including leading development functions and managing fundraising professionals.
* Demonstrated success securing major gifts, ideally at the five\-, six\-, and seven\-figure levels.
* Proven ability to build fundraising strategies that produce measurable revenue growth.
* Experience across major gifts, individual giving, corporate and foundation relations, events, stewardship, and campaign planning.
* Skilled at partnering with CEOs, Boards, major donors, and community leaders.
* Experience with CRM systems, pipeline development, forecasting, and metrics\-driven management.
* Strong financial acumen and excellent communication and relationship\-building skills.
* Experience in healthcare, homelessness, housing, or human services preferred.
* Meaningful connections within Orange County and/or Southern California a plus.

 **Who you are**  

  

You are an entrepreneurial, relationship\-oriented fundraising leader who pairs a strong track record of results with genuine care for people. You lead with kindness, humility, and accountability, you are comfortable rolling up your sleeves alongside your team, and you bring energy, creativity, and a genuine commitment to our mission.

 **Benefits**

* Medical Insurance funded up to 91% by Illumination Foundation (Kaiser and Blue Shield), depending on the plan
* Dental and Vision Insurance
* Life, AD\&D and LTD Insurance funded 100% by Illumination Foundation
* Employee Assistance Program
* Professional Development Reimbursement

jobs.description:
**Program Overview**


Community Solutions, Inc. is seeking a dedicated a passionate candidate to fill the role of Program Director for our Multi\-Dimensional Anti\-Recidivism Partnership (MAP) located in San Bernardino, CA. The selected candidate will be leading and managing the daily operations of the program through recruiting, training, and providing supervision and development to staff members, while ensuring that the program is operating in a manner that exemplifies CSI's values, including principles of diversity, equity and inclusion. MAP is an innovative program dedicated to engaging the community and providing rehabilitative programming for justice\-involved individuals. We focus on promoting long\-term, self\-sustaining skills through vocational training and personal development services. This unique model hosts a variety of sub\-contractors at one site to reduce barriers for clients.

**Position Overview**

* Review and approve all staff duties and client paperwork including but not limited to, program plans, monthly progress reports, closing summaries, and counseling forms.
* Conduct, with the assistance of any supervisory staff, recruitment for all program positions.
* Conduct and facilitate staff orientation and training using in\-service and outside agency resources.
* Ensure supervised staff receive a minimum of required hours of training annually.
* Monitor program and staff compliance with all agency policy and procedure.
* Ensure compliance with other relevant criteria including referring agency requirements and applicable standards.
* Perform policy and program audits as required.
* Evaluate program effectiveness and cost\-efficiency.
* Review weekly sanitation and safety inspection reports and address deficiencies.
* Monitor on an ongoing basis program expense and revenue budget categories.
* Maintain monthly documentation on above and justify variations from budget averages targeted.
* Develop annual program budget and establish fiscal priorities.
* Ensure proper accountability over program resources including food, utilities, telephone, and house and office supplies.
* Approve and coordinate client referrals and intakes from respective contracting agencies.
* Identify, coordinate and monitor existing and new outside agency resources for program and agency use.
* Develop contacts with outside agencies and individuals which may foster agency and program growth.
* Perform the functions of Human Service Worker or Case Manager that relate to client supervision, treatment and custody as needed.
* Directly investigate and handle all client appeals of a disciplinary or grievance nature.
* Coordinate and participate in all client admissions, orientation, and removals.
* The Program Director should be ready to perform any tasks, reasonably assigned, that are needed to maintain the viability of the Program.

**Qualifications:**

* A Master's degree and three years of experience, or a Bachelor's degree and five years of experience in the social service or criminal justice field. Education may be substituted with relevant experience on a one\-year\-for\-one\-year basis.
* Three years of experience in management and supervision of staff.
* Ability to engage and develop collaborations with community agencies.
* Previous assessment and experience with Microsoft Office preferred.

**Benefits:**

**Generous Time Off:** 2 weeks of vacation for first year (increasing to 3 weeks after 1 year), 7 days of sick time, and 4 floating holidays.

**Health \& Wellness:** Medical, dental, and voluntary vision plans, plus FSA, short\-term disability, accident insurance, hospital coverage, life insurance, and AD\&D options.

**401(k) Retirement Plan:** Automatic enrollment with a 100% company match up to 4%.

**Professional Development:** Tuition reimbursement after 1 year, plus ongoing training and opportunities for certification.




**Annual Salary:** The salary range for this position starts at $85,000 and the offer will be reflective of experience, education, skillset, etc.

**Company Overview:**

Community Solutions Inc. (CSI) is a nonprofit organization that promotes the responsible citizenship, accountability, and well\-being of individuals and families involved, or at risk of involvement, in the child welfare, juvenile justice, or criminal justice system. Since CSIs founding in 1962, it has been a pioneer in the community\-based service. We have been delivering supervision, treatment, and comprehensive individualized services to help clients interact more effectively in their communities and become productive citizens. Using this plan, we built the first ever halfway house in New England which has now been replicated and grown to almost 50 programs in 9 states. For over 50 years, CSI has been building upon its successful foundations and has been expanding its services to serve thousands of adults, youth, and families each year.


**CSI is an Equal Opportunity Employer – M/F/Disability/Vet. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.**
